notes: Yarbrough 2009 Science (PMID via DOI). Quote is verbatim first sentence of abstract. Organism V. parahaemolyticus matches. BUT abstract only labels VopS a "type III effector" and characterizes AMPylation of Rho GTPases; it provides NO experimental secretion/translocation evidence in this ref (no supernatant, no CyaA/BlaM reporter, no machinery-dependent export). Secretion rests on the "effector" label only -> weak per strict rubric. Checked DOI 10.1126/science.1166382 (Crossref + Europe PMC abstract).

Yoshida 2002 EMBO J (PMID 12065406, PMC126072). Quote "VirA is a novel type of bacterial effector capable of inducing membrane ruffling through the stimulation of MT destabilization." is verbatim final sentence of abstract. Abstract documents T3SS delivery: "Shigella deliver a subset of effectors into the host cell via the type III secretion system". Organism Shigella flexneri matches. Checked DOI 10.1093/emboj/cdf319.

Vander Broek 2017 Front Cell Infect Microbiol (PMID 28770177, PMC5515863). Quote "The Burkholderia BipC protein is homologous to the Salmonella SipC and Shigella IpaC T3SS proteins, and is secreted by the Bsa T3SS" appears verbatim as opening sentence of Discussion (full text; species-name italics stripped by fetcher but sentence structure identical). Documents Bsa T3SS secretion. Organism B. pseudomallei K96243 matches (BipC = BPSS1531). Checked DOI 10.3389/fcimb.2017.00333.

Matsumoto 2005 Mol Microbiol. Both quote fragments verbatim in abstract: "Eight of these Ysps (YspK, YspI, YspE, YspF, YspP, YspY, YspN and YspL) had not previously been characterized" and "...resulted in Ysa T3S system-dependent increases in cytosolic levels of cAMP for six Ysps (YspK, YspI, YspE, YspF, YspP and YspL)". Documents Ysa T3SS-dependent translocation via Ysp-CyaA cAMP reporter. Organism Y. enterocolitica 8081/Biovar 1B matches. uniprot field is "-" in input, echoed verbatim. Checked DOI 10.1111/j.1365-2958.2005.04973.x (Crossref + Europe PMC).

Tu 2003 Mol Microbiol. Quote "EspH is translocated efficiently into the infected cells by the TTSS and localizes beneath the EPEC microcolonies." is verbatim in abstract. Documents T3SS/TTSS translocation. Row organism EPEC E2348/69; paper covers EPEC+EHEC -> organism match yes. Checked DOI 10.1046/j.1365-2958.2003.03329.x (Crossref + Europe PMC).

Tobe 2006 PNAS (PMID 16990433, PMC1595455) on EHEC O157:H7 Sakai. Quote cites Table 1 title "Summary of E. coli O157:H7 effectors" (verbatim) + effector-column entry "NleD"; NleD listed in Table 1 as experimentally confirmed effector (evidence code B = beta-lactamase translocation). Documents T3SS translocation. Row organism/uniprot is EPEC E2348/69 (B7UNX6) but ref is EHEC Sakai O157:H7 -> strain_diff (conserved Nle effector across EPEC/EHEC; the rubric's canonical accepted case). Checked DOI 10.1073/pnas.0604891103, PMC1595455 Table 1.

Knutton 1998 EMBO J (PMID 9545230, PMC1170561). Quote "In EPEC, four proteins are known to be exported by a type III secretion system_EspA, EspB and EspD required for subversion of host cell signal transduction pathways" matches abstract verbatim (the "_" stands for an em dash in original: "...secretion system--EspA, EspB and EspD..."). Documents T3SS export of EspA. Row organism is Citrobacter rodentium ICC168 (D2TKE3); ref is EPEC -> strain_diff (EspA is a conserved LEE/A-E effector shared by EPEC/EHEC/C. rodentium). Checked DOI 10.1093/emboj/17.8.2166.
